subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that refers to the underlined segment in the given sentence.

His father __enjoyed the strongest position __as an MLA in his constituency.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. "To get upper hand".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"To get upper hand"** means to gain advantage, control, or dominance over someone or something. (प्रभुत्व प्राप्त करना)

 
 
• **Example:** The team worked hard to get the upper hand in the match and eventually won.
 
 
 
• The word **"To get upper hand"** fits the context of the sentence, as it emphasizes the father’s strong position as an MLA, implying dominance or advantage. (प्रभुत्व की स्थिति)
 
 
• **Example:** His father enjoyed the strongest position as an MLA, clearly having the upper hand in his constituency.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: To be at one's wit** (चिंतित या असमंजस में): Refers to being at a point of extreme anxiety or confusion.

 
 
• **Example:** He was at his wit's end trying to solve the complex puzzle.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: To be at hem of** (प्रारंभिक स्थिति में होना): Refers to being at the beginning or under control of someone.
 
 
• **Example:** She was at the hem of her career when she joined the company.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: To go to the dogs** (बर्बादी की ओर जाना): Refers to a situation deteriorating or becoming worse.
 
 
• **Example:** After the company’s leadership changed, its business started going to the dogs.
